title: AffinityTune: A Prompt-Tuning Framework for Few-Shot Anomaly Detection on Graphs

problem.claim: Graph anomaly detection is hindered by scarce labeled anomalies, limitations of unsupervised methods, and weak knowledge transfer in semi-supervised and few-shot approaches.

gap.claim: Prompt tuning on graphs remains underexplored for anomaly detection on heterophilous graphs.

contributions.claim: AffinityTune provides a unified affinity-judgment framework for few-shot graph anomaly detection.
The framework uses multi-granularity tasks comparing nodes with adjacent subgraphs and communities to learn diverse anomaly priors.
FlexPrompt is a flexible prompt-tuning strategy paired with learnable task heads for fine-grained downstream adaptation and task synergy.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors describe AffinityTune as a novel framework for few-shot graph anomaly detection based on prompt tuning.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments on real-world and synthetic datasets reportedly show that AffinityTune significantly outperforms existing methods in detection efficacy.

narrative_sequence.summary: Graph anomaly detection is important across networking, finance, and bioinformatics, but labeled anomalies are scarce.
Existing semi-supervised, few-shot, and graph prompt-tuning approaches leave knowledge-transfer and heterophilous-graph challenges insufficiently addressed.
AffinityTune introduces affinity-based multi-granularity tasks, a global-representation affinity formulation, learnable task heads, and FlexPrompt.
The authors report improved detection efficacy on real-world and synthetic datasets.

source_observation.claim: The framework decomposes anomaly detection into affinity judgments at multiple graph granularities.

interpretation.claim: Combining local, community-level, and global representations may provide complementary anomaly priors for few-shot adaptation.

application.claim: Few-shot graph anomaly detectors could consider multi-granularity affinity tasks when labeled anomalies are limited.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish which graph types, anomaly distributions, or task components are necessary for the reported improvement.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the datasets, baselines, evaluation metrics, or numerical results.
The abstract does not quantify parameter efficiency or describe the heterophilous graph settings used.
The abstract does not report ablations separating the contributions of the multi-granularity tasks, task heads, and FlexPrompt.
